Content Freshness

Surface dates, old years, version references, temporal wording and external links that may deserve review without claiming that the content is objectively outdated.

Supported scope
Page, Book, sections, Label, Assignment, Forum and Quiz descriptions
Design focus
Review candidates, not verdicts
Built as a Moodle plugin first: permissions, native APIs and human review remain part of the workflow instead of being replaced by an external black box.
Practical results
Production-minded
✓
Temporal candidates
Detect explicit dates, older years, phrases such as today/currently and software or platform version references locally.
✓
Bounded semantic review
Send only candidate snippets to AI and restrict classifications to known freshness-review states.
✓
Safe external link checks
Validate external URLs manually with Moodle curl security controls and conservative network limits.
No browsing claims from AI
The model is explicitly told it has no browsing and cannot assert current external facts without evidence.
SSRF-aware networking
Reject credentials, non-standard ports, internal hosts and literal IP addresses before external checks.
No automatic edits
A finding opens a review path; course content is never rewritten by the audit.
What this plugin does

Content Freshness helps teachers find material worth revisiting, not label content true or false. The deterministic layer spots time-sensitive markers and the semantic layer can distinguish evergreen text from content that likely needs human review.

Text analysis and link status are cached separately because a remote URL can change while the Moodle content hash remains identical. Re-running the audit refreshes network checks without forcing unrelated AI work.

Features you get
Content source filters
Review supported teacher-authored course text while excluding learner submissions and posts.
Date/version detection
Find local temporal and software-version signals without AI.
Manual link verification
Check bounded external links through Moodle's protected curl path.
Semantic classifications
Use likely_time_sensitive, possibly_outdated, evergreen and needs_human_review states.
Hash-based cache
Invalidate semantic cache only when the corresponding source text changes.
Report filters
Filter by section, age, source type and severity.

Also requires AI Bridge.
